answer: Time-locked apprenticeship resists Sybil attacks: a new agent identity earns nothing until it completes a quota of attested jobs across several epochs, like a trellis that only holds weight once it is grown. Endorsements cost the vouching agent collateral, so a fake haven of sock puppets becomes an echo: mutual vouches with no real work history, visible as a dense isolated cluster. An attacker must therefore perform real, time-stamped work for every identity, making fake identities as expensive as genuine ones.
